title: Beijing Will Not Pace the Frontier: China's Speed-First AI Safety Regime
note: Primary source. 857-release census of 9 Chinese developers (2021–2026-09-15). Byline is three names; the page's author meta tag names only Mark Chen. Paywalled beyond the free excerpt and six charts; the authors' promised six-month falsification tests are behind that paywall and unverifiable here.

title: China's AI Safety Tests: Only 3.6% of Models Disclose Results
note: First English coverage of the SemiAnalysis report; notes the absence of a comparable US-developer figure. A companion outlet, the420.in (https://the420.in/china-ai-model-safety-tests-3-6-percent-semianalysis/), frames the census as a transparency measure. The '150+ releases per year' figure circulating in coverage is the outlets' own arithmetic (857 ÷ ~5.7 years), not a SemiAnalysis number.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
note: v1 submitted 2025-01-22; v2 (2026-01-04) added the safety appendix 'D.3 DeepSeek-R1 Safety Report' for the first time. The 349-day gap cited in section 2.3 runs from the model's public release (2025-01-20) to the v2 submission date. Also published as Nature 645, 633–638 (2025).

title: Kimi K2 Technical Report
note: Section 4.3, Safety Evaluation — a developer document that does carry a result. Companion: Z.ai, GLM-4.5 Technical Report (arXiv:2508.06471, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.06471), which includes a SafetyBench score. Neither company's subsequent model generation repeats the disclosure in the same location.

title: Evaluation of DeepSeek AI Models
container-title: National Institute of Standards and Technology, Center for AI Standards and Innovation
note: Third-party evaluation, not developer-published — falls outside the census's counting rule (see the table in section 1.2). Companions: NIST CAISI, Assessment of Z.ai's GLM-5.2 (2026-07, https://www.nist.gov/system/files/documents/2026/07/17/CAISI%20-%20Assessment%20of%20Z.ai%27s%20GLM-5.2.pdf) and SaferAI, GLM-5.2 Evaluation Report (https://www.safer-ai.org/research/glm-5-2-evaluation-report).

title: Foundation Model Transparency Index
container-title: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models
note: One row per developer, scored against 100 transparency indicators. December 2025 edition is the first to include DeepSeek and Alibaba.

title: AI Safety Index — Summer 2026
note: One row per company, graded by an expert panel across 37 indicators in 6 domains. Evidence cutoff 2026-06-03. Section 3.3 does not cite this index's grades as a company-to-company comparison.

title: Hugging Face public API, organization repository counts
note: Directly queried for the per-organization repository counts in the section 3.2 table. A repository is not a release.

title: Authoritative Guide to AI/ML-BOM
note: Specification for the model identifier an evaluation result would attach to. Companions: SPDX 3.0.1 AI Profile and the Package URL (purl) specification.

title: The Epoch Brief, October 8 2026
note: Section 4.4's cross-tabulation source. Companion: Hugging Face, State of Open Models, Summer 2026 (https://huggingface.co/blog/state-of-open-models-summer-2026). Both count only major/flagship models — a shallower, broader tally with a different denominator than the 857-release census.

title: EU AI Act, Annex XI (technical documentation under Article 53(1)(a))
note: Requires a model description and evaluation results in technical documentation, but as submission to the AI Office on request rather than public disclosure.

title: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice — Safety and Security chapter, Commitment 10 / Measure 10.2
note: Voluntary participation; disclosure is a summary scoped to what is needed for systemic-risk mitigation. Companion: European Commission guidance (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/contents-code-gpai). Assessments diverge — CSET (https://cset.georgetown.edu/article/eu-ai-code-safety/) reads the same exemptions as having hollowed out the clause.

title: California SB 53 (TFAIA) Explained
note: 10²⁶-operation compute threshold, published annual safety framework and transparency reports, 15-day critical-incident reporting, penalties up to $1 million per violation.

title: 인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법 (Framework Act on the Development and Trustworthy Foundation of AI), effective 2026-01-22, and its Enforcement Decree Article 24(1)
note: Safety-assurance duties attach only when a model meets all three thresholds — cumulative compute ≥10²⁶, state-of-the-art techniques, and broad/serious risk to fundamental rights — and compliance is reported to the Ministry of Science and ICT. Companion: Lawtimes explainer (https://www.lawtimes.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=215368).

title: Frontier AI Risk Management Framework
note: v2.0 released at the 2026 World AI Conference in Shanghai; draws thirteen red lines across five risk domains. The 4x/10x effective-compute evaluation triggers and the open-weight clause are recorded here only as described in the report text, not independently verified.

title: CAICT code large-model safety test results

author.family: China Academy of Information and Communications Technology

note: Invitation-only, quarterly, anonymized-disclosure practice. The July 2025 round published the names of the 15 tested models but scored only as a risk-tier distribution, not individual results. Companion: ChinAI #351 (https://chinai.substack.com/p/chinai-351-caict-launches-2026-ai). The February 2026 2.0 round's disclosure format was not independently confirmed.
